newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty breaks resistance, depo rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty breaks resistance, depo rates rise.

text.p: The zloty pierced strong resistance at three percent from the trading band centre on the back of small foreign client entry into Polish treasuries.

Dealers said that if the market remained in its pro-zloty mood during the next several days the central bank could intervene to push the zloty back under three percent, the levels where it had said it would like to see the zloty trade.

"The supply of currencies on the market was not very large today but foreign investors may continue to enter Polish paper as yields grow, placing upward pressure on the zloty," said Zbigniew Choszcz, senior dealer at Bank Gdanski SA.
The zloty closed at 3.13/3.07 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Friday's 3.03/2.97 percent.
It was at 3.0560/70 to the dollar, up from 3.0580/95 on Friday and flat at 1.8045/65 to the mark.

Market estimates showed that foreign investors bid for $30 million of Polish T-bills at Monday's primary auction. Dealers earlier said that foreigners also had to pay for fixed bonds bought last month before the March 5 value date.
At auction all minimum prices fell with the average yield of the benchmark 52-week T-bill rising to 20.92 percent, up from 20.47 percent last week.

On the money market one-day rates inched up on Monday as banks built up positions fearing lower liquidity after the central bank increased obligatory reserves on zloty and currency deposits from the start of the month, dealers said.
Overnight rates closed at 22.70/23.20 percent, up from opening's 22.20/22.60 percent. Tomorrow/next rates increased to 22.80/23.20 percent from 22.25/22.70.
Some dealers said liquidity would likely rise later this week as the shock impact of higher reserves wears off.
